facts.summary: California requires daily overtime: 1.5x after 8 hours in a workday and 2x after 12, plus 1.5x after 40 in a week and rules for the 7th consecutive day. The rule that pays more applies.
facts.sourceAgency: California Dept of Industrial Relations, DLSE

facts.summary: California's white-collar exemption salary floor is 2x the state minimum wage for full-time work — about $1,352/week in 2026 — higher than the federal $684. Failing the state floor means overtime is owed even if the federal test passes.
facts.citation: Cal. Lab. Code § 515(a); IWC Wage Orders
facts.sourceAgency: California Dept of Industrial Relations, DLSE
facts.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-08: derived as 2 x state minimum wage x 40 hrs x 52 / 12 = 2 x $16.90 x 40 x 52 / 12 = $1,352.00/week, using the confirmed-current $16.90 state minimum wage (see minimumWage.hourly, sourced to DIR News Release 2025-118). Figure checks out arithmetically against the confirmed rate.

facts.summary: California's computer-professional exemption sets a much higher pay floor than the federal $27.63/hour: for 2026 the exemption requires at least $58.85/hour (or $10,214.44/month, or $122,573.13/year) in salary/wages; a worker exempt federally may still be owed overtime under California law if paid below this rate.
facts.sourceAgency: California Dept of Industrial Relations, Office of Policy, Research and Legislation
facts.notes: Confirmed directly from DIR's own computer-software-exemption page: DIR adjusted the rate from $56.97 to $58.85/hr (monthly $9,888.13 to $10,214.44; annual $118,657.43 to $122,573.13), effective January 1, 2026, reflecting the CPI-W increase. DIR re-adjusts this rate every October 1 for the following January 1 -- re-check annually.

facts.summary: California state minimum wage (indexed annually). Many localities set a higher wage that applies instead.
facts.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-08 directly against DIR News Release No. 2025-118, confirming the state minimum wage increased from $16.50 to $16.90/hour effective January 1, 2026 (indexed under Labor Code 1182.12). No longer provisional. Many localities set a higher local minimum wage that applies instead -- re-check annually as this is indexed for inflation.

value: and more (in addition to federal classes)
facts.summary: California's FEHA covers all federal protected classes plus additional categories, and applies to more employers than federal law.
FEHA covers employers with 5 or more employees; the harassment provisions apply to employers of any size.
Once accommodation is requested (no magic words needed), the employer must engage in a good-faith interactive process; failing to do so is itself a violation. Applies at 5+ employees.
California protects employees from retaliation for reporting suspected legal violations or refusing to participate in them.
facts.sourceAgency: California Dept of Industrial Relations, DLSE

facts.summary: California allows 3 years to bring statutory wage claims, and up to 4 years under the Unfair Competition Law.
facts.citation: Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 338; Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17208
facts.sourceAgency: California Dept of Industrial Relations, DLSE

facts.summary: A FEHA complaint must be filed with the Civil Rights Department within 3 years of the alleged violation, followed by a right-to-sue.
Already-earned wages generally cannot be waived in a release; a severance release does not extinguish overtime already owed.
facts.sourceAgency: California Dept of Industrial Relations, DLSE
